IS I 9812 - 1981

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR CANNED SPINACH
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 April 1981, after the draft finalized by the Fruits and Vegetables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Canned spinach is the product prepared from mature spinach of suitable varieties. They are cleaned and packed in brine. They are processed in appropriate manner before and after being sealed in containers So as to prevent spoilage. 0..3 There is ample scope for development of trade in canned spinach. In order to ensure quality of the product, it is necessary to have strict quality control based on specifications. It was, therefore, felt necessary to formulate an Indian Standard Specification for the product. 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954; the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955; and the Fruit Products Order, 1955. However, this standard is subject to the restriction imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressoff in accordance ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded The number of significant places retained in the with IS: 2-1960*. rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. 2.3.1 Blemished Unit - Unit that is blemished with some injury, such as wormhole, insect damage, physiological disorder or other abnormality such as sun burn, scab and enzyme activity on the surface, readily visible to the naked eye to a noticeable degree. A unit shall be considered blemished when the aggregate blemished area exceeds the area of a circle Uneven distribution of pigments and changes 0.32 cm in diameter. in colour normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. 2.4 Can Round open top sanitary cans conforming shall be individual to IS : 9396-1979t. leaves of spinach 3. STYLES 3.1 The spinach used for canning without any stalk. 4. GRADES 4.1 Canned spinach shall be of two grades, namely Grade 1 and Grade 2.

5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Hygienic Requirements - The material shall be prepared and handled under strict hygienic conditions ( see IS : 6542-19721 ) by persons free from contagious and infectious diseases and only in premises maintained in thoroughly clean and hygienic conditions and having adequate and safe water supply. All workers shall use clean, white, washed clothing. Necessary precautions shall be taken to prevent incidental contamination of the product from soiled equipment or from personnel suffering from injuries. 5.1.1 All equipment coming in contact with raw materials or products in the course of manufacture shall be kept clean. An ample supply of steam and water, and hose, brushes and other equipment necessary for proper cleaning of machinery and equipment shall be available, The equipment shall be properly cleaned by suitable chlorine solution having at least 50 mg/kg of available chlorine.
*Method of sampling and test for processed fruits and vegetables. $Specification for round open top sanitary cans. $Code for hygienic conditions for fruit and vegetable canning units.

4

IS : 9812 - 1981
5.2 General - The ` spinach ' selected for canning shall be of good quality, of the proper stage of maturity and shall have the characteristic colour, flavour and texture, and shall be free from blemishes and damage by insects or disease. Colour of leaves shall not be yellow. Texture of leave shall not be fibrous. Spinach used should be of the same variety. 5.3 Freedom from Preservatives, Artificial Colouring Matter and Flavouring Agents - The material shall be free from any preservative, artificial colouring matter or flavouring agents, 5.4 Requirements for Covering Brine - The The only substance that may be added clear. edible common salt ( sodium chloride ) between without small quantity of sucrose, and citric or permitted acidulents not exceeding 0.1 percent of covering brine shall be to the covering brine is 1 to 2 percent, with or tartaric acid or other the packing medium. contents of the

5.5 Requirements for the Finished Product - The can on opening shall display the following characteristics:

Grade 1 - The material shall possess a good, characteristic and practically uniform colour; shall be practically free from defects; shall possess a good texture and characteristic flavour; shall be free from grit and dirt; and shall be of such quality with respect to clarity of covering liquor as to score not less than 85 points. material shall possess a characteristic and 2 - The reasonably uniform colour; shall be reasonably free from defects; shall possess a reasonably good texture and characteristic flavour; shall be free from grit and dirt; and shall be of such quality with respect to clarity of covering liquor as to score not less than 75 points.

5.5.2 Colour

a) Grade 1 - The leaves shall possess a good, practically uniform colour, characteristic of spinach of the proper maturity, which means that the colour of the leaves shall be green to pale green but not yellowish, indicative of very mature leaves. Uneven distribution of pigments and change in colour normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. uniform b) Grade 2 - The leaves shall possess a good, reasonably colour, characteristic of spinach at the right stage of maturity, which means that the colour of the leaves shall be green to pale Uneven green but not yellowish, indicative of very mature units. distribution of pigments and change in colour normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. 5.5.3 Texture texture, good a) Grade 1 - The leaves shall possess practically which means the leaves shall be just soft but not fibrous. b) Grade 2 - The leaves shall possess a reasonably which means that the leaves shall be reasonably fibrous.

5.5.4 Taste and F/avow taste and a) Grade I - The leaves shall possess the characteristic flavour of the canned spinach in brine. The leaves shall be practically devoid of any objectionable or off-taste, or objectionable smell and odour. b) Grade 2 - The leaves shall possess the characteristic taste and flavour of the canned spinach in brine. The leaves shall be reasonably devoid of any objectionable or off-taste or objectionable smell and odour. 5.5.5 Absence of Defects a) Grade I - The leaves shall be practically free from defects, which means that there shall not be present an extraneous material like the stems and there shall be present not more than The covering brine shall be thin, 5 percent of blemished leaves. practically clear and practically free from cloudiness and suspended matter. b) Grade 2 - The leaves shall be reasonably free from defects, which means that there shall not be present an extraneous material like the stems and there shall be present not more than 10 percent of blemished leaves. The covering brine shall be thin, reasonably clear and reasonably free from cloudiness and suspended matter.

6. PACKING

AND MARKING

6.1 Packing - The material shall be packed in cans made of electrolytic The cans shall be either plain or internally or any other suitable tinplate. The side seam shall be externally side lacquered and hermetically sealed. The lacquer used internally shall be nonstripped with suitable lacquer. The exterior of toxic, acid-resistant and conforming to IS : 5818-1970*. the can shall be free from dents, rust, perforations and seam distortions. The interior of the The cans shall not show leaking, panelling or swell. lacquered cans shall not show any visible black discolouration, rusting or The interior of pitting and the inside lacquer shall be in good condition. the plain cans may show visible black discolouration. Normal feathering shall not be considered as a defect.

APPENDIX A ( Clause 5.5. I )
METHOD A-l. GENERAL OF SCORING

A-l.1 Scoring of the product shall be done by a panel of three to five judges. All the judges constituting a panel shall be conversant with the factors covering the quality of the product. The cans shall be opened and contents poured separately into white porcelain bowls. Each judge shall independently examine the contents from each of the cans and assign scores for different characteristics.
A-l.2 The judges taste and flavour, A-2. SCORING shall consider the characteristics, and absence of defects. buchas colour, texture,

A-2.1 System of described that the numerically. The numerically on a individual factors, his observations in

Scoring - The variations within each factor are so scores may be ascertained for each factor and expressed relative importance of each factor has been expressed scale of 100. Each judge shall give a score for the by the method described in Table 3 and record the score sheet for individual judge.

A-2.1.1 The scores as number of points given on the score sheet by the judges for the contents of each can for the four factors shall be recorded in a tabular form in the score card and the average score calculated for
*Method of sampling and test for processed tSpecification for apple juice. fruits and vegetables.

9

IS:9812-1981 each factor with overall average column of the score card after in A-2.2.1 and A-2.2.2. A-2.2 Ascertaining the Score for each can entered in the appropriate complying with the conditions specified

the consistency of A-2.2.1 Agreement among Judges - To ascertain judgement among the judges, the total score assigned by each of them for the contents of the same can shall be calculated by adding up the scores for the various individual characteristics. If the difference between the maximum and the minimum of the total score so obtained does not exceed ( K + 5 ), where K is the number of judges, the scoring shall be deemed as consistent for the can under consideration. If the difference exceeds ( K -+ 5 ), the most outlying score, that is, the one which is farthest from its immediate neighbour ( the scores being arranged in one order ), shall be discarded and the consistency among the remaining judges shall be examined. A-2.2.2 When the consistency is thus established ( A-2.2.1 ), the overall average scores given by the judges, whose scoring has been found to be consistent, shall be calculated for each can. The average score for each of the individual characteristics shall also be calculated by taking into account the corresponding scores as given by the same judges for the contents of the same can. NO. 1 MAY 1996 TO IS 9812 : 1981 SPECIFICATION FOR CANNED SPINACH ( Page 3, Foreword, clause 0.4 ) and renumber tbe subsequent clause:
Add the following new clause after 0.4

AMENDMENT

`0.5 A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECO-Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO-Mark shall be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Acr, 1986 as per tbe Resolution No. 71 dated 20 February 1991 and Resolution No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with the ECO-Mark it shall also carry the Standard Mark of BIS for quality besides meeting additional environment friendly (EF) requirements. The environment friendly requirements for canned spinach are, therefore, included through Amendment No. 1 to this standard. This amendment is based on the Gazette Notification No. 624 (E) dated 6 September 1995 for Labelling Beverages, Infant Foods, Processed Fruits and Vegetable Products as environment friendly, published in the Gazette of the Government of India .' (Page 7, clause 55.6 ) "5.6 Additional Requirements Add the following for ECO-Mark new clause after 55.6:

5.6.1 General Requirements 5.6.1.1 The product shall conform to 5.5.6. to the requirements prescribed under 5.1

5.6.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce the consent clearance as per the provisions of Water (PCP) Act, 1974, Water (PCP) Cess Act, 1977 and Air (PCP) Act, 1981 along with the authorization if required under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules made thereunder to the Bureau of Indian Standards while applying for the ECO-Mark and the product shall also be in accordance with the Prevetiion of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules made thereunder. Additionally, IT0 1955 (Fruit Product Order) framed under Essential Commodities Act, 1955, Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1977 requirements wherever applicable has to be complied with.
